macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Hot U.S. inflation sends stocks lower and boosts Fed hike bets
items.summary: September CPI rose 0.6% month over month, while annual headline inflation accelerated to 3.7% and core inflation exceeded expectations. The data pushed Treasury yields higher and increased market expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike at its late-October meeting; the Nasdaq fell about 1.4% and the S&P 500 about 1% in Wednesday trading.

items.title: Fed official says another rate increase may be appropriate
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said another interest-rate increase could be appropriate this year, while leaving open the possibility of further policy moves in 2027. His comments reinforced the market’s reaction to the hotter inflation report.

items.title: Bank earnings produce mixed results
items.summary: Morgan Stanley reported better-than-expected results, while Bank of America posted weaker third-quarter profit and revenue. BlackRock beat expectations and rose, whereas State Street declined after revenue missed forecasts.

items.title: ASML raises annual outlook amid AI chip-equipment demand
items.summary: ASML increased its annual forecast for the third time this year, citing strong demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment linked to artificial-intelligence infrastructure.

items.title: Japan’s central bank seen resisting immediate back-to-back rate hike
items.summary: Bank of Japan officials reportedly lean against raising rates again this month, while retaining the possibility of another increase as soon as December. The outlook influenced yen trading and broader Asian-market sentiment.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin dips below $82,000 as inflation and oil prices pressure markets
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below $82,000 as higher oil prices contributed to hotter U.S. inflation data and rising bond yields. Ether and several major altcoins also weakened amid broader risk aversion.

items.title: South Korea blocks 27 unregistered crypto exchange websites
items.summary: South Korean authorities approved blocking domestic access to 27 websites operated by unregistered exchanges, including KuCoin, MEXC, Phemex and Bitrue, and referred dozens of operators for investigation.

items.title: SEC enables framework for crypto multi-asset trust options
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission made operative a Cboe BZX rule change establishing a framework for options on commodity-based trusts holding multiple crypto assets.

items.title: Ripple partners with Korean securities firm on custody and tokenization
items.summary: Ripple announced a strategic partnership with Meritz Securities to explore using Ripple Custody and its tokenization infrastructure in South Korea’s capital markets.

items.title: Standard Chartered launches direct Bitcoin and Ether trading in UAE
items.summary: Standard Chartered introduced direct Bitcoin and Ether trading for affluent clients in the United Arab Emirates, describing it as the bank’s first direct crypto-trading service for wealthy customers in any market.

items.title: Pons token rises about 15% in 24 hours
items.summary: Pons, the native token of the Robinhood Chain launchpad, traded around $0.353, up approximately 15% over 24 hours and reaching a market capitalization near $238 million.

items.title: EasyA reaches $1.1 billion valuation and targets public listing
items.summary: Blockchain education and developer platform EasyA reportedly reached a $1.1 billion valuation and is targeting a 2027 public listing involving tokenized shares.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: Google released Gemini 4 Argon for coding, knowledge work, enterprise workflows and cyber defense. It is available through paid Gemini APIs and several Google consumer and developer products.

items.title: Meta introduces Muse Wonder models
items.summary: Meta launched Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, frontier models aimed at complex agentic tasks. The company says they compete with leading models, though independent validation was not identified.

items.title: OpenAI expands GPT-6 lineup
items.summary: OpenAI reportedly introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, targeting higher-end coding and agentic workloads and lower-cost, high-volume use cases respectively. The models are reportedly available through the API and selected ChatGPT, Work and Codex plans.

items.title: Anthropic and Nvidia back Basecamp Research
items.summary: Anthropic and Nvidia participated in a $140 million funding round for Basecamp Research, reflecting continued investment in AI-related scientific and biological data infrastructure.

items.title: NEURA Robotics launches Neuron AI
items.summary: German robotics company NEURA Robotics introduced Neuron AI, a multimodal foundation model for physical AI that combines 3D vision, touch, audio, robot state, language and memory for humanoid-robot applications.

items.title: Nvidia open-sources Run:ai platform
items.summary: Nvidia open-sourced the full Run:ai platform under its DSX AI Factory initiative, allowing organizations to deploy the integrated platform or adopt individual components for AI infrastructure management.

items.title: Prime Intellect acquires Moondream
items.summary: Prime Intellect acquired Moondream and plans to integrate its open vision models and inference optimizations into Prime’s multimodal training and deployment stack. Financial terms were not disclosed.

items.title: OpenAI reports insider-security investigation
items.summary: OpenAI said it used its own models while investigating a concealed recording device allegedly planted by an employee, terminated the employee and referred the matter to the FBI. The company said it found no current indication of unauthorized access to weights, source code or customer data.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Microsoft launches Xbox Labs for browser and cross-device gaming
items.summary: Microsoft introduced Xbox Labs, a small team focused on adapting games—including new and classic titles—for browsers and devices beyond traditional Xbox hardware. The company did not announce specific products, pricing, or release dates.

items.title: Ubisoft Singapore lays off 70 employees after Assassin’s Creed success
items.summary: Ubisoft has reportedly cut 70 jobs at Ubisoft Singapore, about three months after Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced launched successfully. The game reportedly sold two million copies on its first day and three million within a week.

items.title: Nvidia announces faster DLSS 5 model
items.summary: Nvidia said an updated DLSS 5 neural-rendering model doubles performance, halves GPU overhead, and reduces 4K VRAM use by 20% compared with the September version. It is scheduled to debut in NBA 2K27 on October 16, followed by Hogwarts Legacy and Yanyun Sixteen Sounds.

items.title: GTA VI pre-orders reportedly exceed six million
items.summary: A report claims Grand Theft Auto VI has surpassed six million pre-orders more than a month before its scheduled November 19 release. The figure has not been independently confirmed by Rockstar Games or Take-Two Interactive.

items.title: Battlefield 6 begins its fifth content season
items.summary: Electronic Arts launched Battlefield 6’s fifth season of content on October 13, accompanied by a new gameplay trailer and additional seasonal material.

items.title: Gears of War: E-Day releases on Xbox, PC, and Game Pass
items.summary: Microsoft announced the full release of Gears of War: E-Day for Xbox Series X|S and PC, with availability through Xbox Game Pass Ultimate.

items.title: G-STAR faces major exhibitor absences ahead of GTA VI release
items.summary: South Korea’s G-STAR game exhibition is reportedly contending with reduced participation from major domestic publishers and competition from the November 19 release of GTA VI. Several Chinese companies are expected to attend despite skipping Tokyo Game Show.
